pageCache.pageTitle: Westbury Infant School and Resource Base - Headteacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to the website of Westbury Infant School. My name is Stacey Budge, and I am very proud to be the Headteacher of this school.
I have 3 children of my own and understand how important it is as parent to feel confident about your child’s school and trust the staff to take care of them, as well as teaching them to read, write and count.
At Westbury Infant School, we have an exceptionally caring, family atmosphere where we know children really well, and care about each one of them as an individual. This ethos extends to the whole family and we are always available to support you in any way we can.
We are privileged to share this time with your child and ensure that the foundation skills of literacy and numeracy are taught effectively within a playful and creative curriculum.
Westbury Infant School is the only infant school in Westbury. This means that we are the only school in Westbury that specializes in the Early Education of children. Children develop a huge amount during the ages of 4-7 and as Early Years educators, we are privileged to share this time with your child and ensure that the foundation skills of literacy and numeracy are taught effectively within a playful and creative curriculum.
Our staff are very highly skilled and each class has a full time Teaching Assistant as well as a Teacher. Many children also benefit from additional adult support in small groups or 1:1 as needed. Westbury Infant School benefits from a Resource Base for up to 20 children with complex needs. These children have their own classroom and staff but also spend timetabled sessions with a linked mainstream class.
At Westbury Infant School, we have an exceptionally caring, family atmosphere where we know children really well, and care about each one of them as an individual.
The indoor environment is very well resourced with attractive and stimulating displays. The decoration is neutral and classes are well organized to ensure that bright colours and cluttered shelves do not over stimulate children. The use of natural materials- wood, glass, hessian, enhance this calm atmosphere for learning.Our school is situated in spacious, beautiful grounds for the children to explore and play. There is a large trim trail at the front of the school, a big playground, an adventure playground and a sensory garden.This gives our children fantastic opportunities to extend their learning outside the classroom and plenty of space for playtimes.
We offer the children a rich, broad and balanced curriculum which is further enhanced with lots of school trips and visitors. We plan 4 main trips each year, which are closely linked to the curricuulm planning. This means that across the 3 years that children learn in our school, they will have a minimum of 12 enrichment trips which are carefully planned to widen their life experiences and support their learning e.g visits to museums, galleries, theatres.
Emotional wellbeing is vital for young children to learn, grow and develop. We provide support for all children through the use of THRIVE. Our family support worker also provides support for parents and carers who need advice or help at any time.
All classrooms have interactive smart boards and Wi-Fi access for iPads and laptops.
Although our children are all very young, the importance of ICT to their leaning is not underestimated. All classrooms have interactive smart boards and Wi-Fi access for iPads and laptops. We have 2 full class sets of iPads which are available for the children to use in their learning.
Lunchtimes are an important part of the day for us at Westbury Infant School. All our children are entitled to a free meal and we see this not only as an opportunity for eating well, but as a sociable occasion. Our children use porcelain plates and real glasses. They are encouraged to pass cutlery to each other and pour their own water when they are able. We have a very high number of Mid Day Supervisory Assistants compared to other schools, which recognizes the importance we place on the care of children at this time. Our daily 3-course menu is cooked on the premises and offers a choice of starter, main course and dessert. Have a look at our latest menu for some ideas of what we offer.
Most children from Westbury Infant School transfer to Westbury Junior School. Our two schools work closely together to ensure that there is a consistency of approach to teaching and assessment. There is a comprehensive transition program to support the children moving from one school to the other.
We hope you gather an insight into life at Westbury Infant School from our website.

Our Vision and Values
We are delighted to share with you our revised vision and values. These have been agreed following consultation with children, staff, governors and parents. Our vision and values are really at the heart of everything we do as a school and what we feel is really important, so we hope you are able to spend a few minutes talking about this with your child/ren.
Our Vision
Belong, Thrive, Achieve, Play- where infants shine every day
Belong “I know I belong to the Westbury Infant School family”Thrive “When we thrive it means we are happy and healthy”Achieve “I try really hard and do my best”Play “We get to learn through play, even in Y2- I love it!”Where infants shine every day “Everyone in our school is a superstar and we all shine together”
Our Values
Our school values support our vision of our school and are an integral part of our ethos and our curriculum. We regularly discuss what our values mean with the children, and they are praised for showing these values during the school day.

New Starters September 2026
Welcome to Westbury Infant School. We are delighted that your child will be joining us and we look forward to meeting you soon.
At Westbury Infants we have a fantastic admin team who will be more than happy to answer any questions or queries you may have.
Please rest assured that we will be working hard to ensure that your child has a settled and happy start to school life at Westbury Infants.
Welcome Letter for New Reception Families
We are delighted to welcome all our new Reception families to Westbury Infant School. A welcome letter has been sent out with important information about starting school, including details of our Parent Induction Evening on Wednesday 10th June 2026 at 5pm.
This meeting is for parents and carers only and is a great opportunity to meet the team and learn more about your child’s transition into school.
Please check your email for the full letter. If you need another copy, feel free to contact the school office.
welcome letter and parents eve invite.pdf
New Starters Transition Dates
We’re delighted to welcome all our new Reception families to Westbury Infant School for September 2026. Our new starter information sets out all the key dates and events that will help your child get to know their teachers, explore their new classroom and begin building those first important connections.
We’re really looking forward to meeting you and your little one as you begin this special journey with us. If you have any questions at all, our friendly school office team is always happy to help.

pageCache.pageTitle: Westbury Infant School and Resource Base - Trips & requests for voluntary contributions
pageCache.text:
Trips & requests for voluntary contributions
We enjoy making the most of our local environment and taking our children on walks and short visits to places of interest in our local area. Parents are asked to sign giving permission for these visits when the children first start at Westbury Infant School.
There will be times when your child will be invited to go on school trips further afield. All school visits are carefully assessed for Health and Safety risks and we ensure that adult to child ratios are maintained at all times.
Parents are asked to make a voluntary contribution towards the cost of the trips to cover the cost of transport and other expenses incurred in providing high quality Learning Outside the Classroom. These experiences supports, enriches and extends learning and development and are much valued by the school as enhancing cultural capital in our learners. It is our intent that all children benefit from these experiences irrespective of the amount of voluntary contribution given. Parents still need to sign the necessary approval slip to participate.
However, an activity may be affected if a significant amount of the cost is not collected. The school would then have to consider cancelling some trips. The school fundraises throughout the year and this money all goes towards subsidizing the cost of trips to parents. All of our trips that cost more that £10 are capped at £10 per child irrespective of how much the trip costs the school.
Parents are informed at the beginning of the academic year when these trips are taking place, so if financial planning is needed, there is time to put this in place. A payment plan can be set up through ParentPay for this very purpose. If you are or believe you will experience further financial difficulty, then please do not hesitate to contact the school as there may be something we can do to help support you with this.

Our Reception Curriculum
Belong, Thrive, Achieve and Play
Reception is an exciting year of discovery, friendship and growing independence. Children become confident members of our school community as they explore new ideas, develop important skills and experience the joy of learning through purposeful play, high-quality teaching and first-hand experiences.
We want every child to feel happy, secure and ready to make the most of all that Reception has to offer.
At Westbury Infant School, we want every child to:
Our values of respect, excellence, resilience, friendship and teamwork are woven throughout the Reception curriculum. They shape our relationships, learning environment and expectations for how children learn and play together.
Belong by feeling safe, included and valued;
Thrive through positive relationships, confidence and wellbeing;
How Children Learn in Reception
Children learn through a carefully balanced combination of:
Teachers identify the important knowledge, skills and vocabulary children need to learn. They teach these directly and plan enhancements that allow children to explore, revisit and apply their learning.
Enhancements may include carefully selected resources, books, vocabulary, questions, problems or experiences. They are chosen purposefully in response to the curriculum and children’s learning needs.
explicit teaching;
purposeful play and exploration;
continuous provision;
planned enhancements to the environment;
high-quality interactions with adults;
first-hand experiences;
practical activities;
stories, songs, poems and rhymes; and
indoor and outdoor learning.
High-Quality Interactions
Adults use the SHREC approach to support children’s communication, language and thinking:
Adults know when to observe, when to join children’s play and when to provide direct teaching or additional support.
Conversation: encouraging meaningful back-and-forth exchanges.
Our Year in Reception
Our curriculum develops progressively across six half terms. New learning builds upon what children already know, while important knowledge and skills are revisited and applied in different contexts.
Autumn 1: Belonging and Noticing Change
Children settle into Reception, build relationships and become familiar with classroom routines.
They explore questions including:
Children talk about themselves, their families and their personal past. They explore the school and local environment, notice early signs of autumn and begin developing early knowledge of number, shape and comparison.
Stories and practical experiences support children to talk about belonging, feelings, friendship and difference.
Key experiences include home visits, joining the school community and exploring the outdoor environment.
How have people grown and changed?
What happens as autumn begins?
Autumn 2: Our Community and Special Times
Children strengthen their relationships, communication and independence.
They explore questions including:
Children learn about people who help within the community and explore different celebrations. They observe seasonal changes and develop their storytelling, sequencing and vocabulary.
Mathematics continues through practical exploration of number, pattern, shape and measure.
Key experiences include a community encounter, the Nativity and Christmas celebrations.
What changes as autumn becomes winter?
Spring 1: Change, the Past and the Wider World
Children develop their questioning, observation and explanation skills.
They explore questions including:
Children compare toys from the past and present using objects, photographs and memories. They encounter contemporary life in India through maps, photographs and information texts.
They investigate freezing and melting, deepen their understanding of materials and develop healthy choices and perseverance.
Key experiences include exploring old and new toys, learning about India and investigating ice and water.
How can objects and materials change?
Spring 2: Growth, Animals and Special Places
Children observe growth and change through sustained first-hand experiences.
They explore questions including:
Children plant and care for seeds, learn about animals and their environments and use non-fiction books to find information.
They learn about Easter and explore why some places are special to Christians. Encounters with other places of worship are supported through stories, images, information or visitors.
Key experiences include planting and caring for seeds, an animal encounter and a visit to All Saints Church.
How do living things grow and change?
What do animals need?
Why are some places special to people?
Summer 1: Journeys, Maps and Life Cycles
Children apply their learning with increasing independence and use more detailed language to explain their ideas.
They explore questions including:
Children observe the caterpillar-to-butterfly life cycle, explore Westbury through a local walk and begin using simple maps.
They use evidence to investigate the local area in the past and present and learn about Mae Jemison as a significant person.
Drawing Club begins during the summer term, giving children opportunities to apply their phonic knowledge and develop their own ideas through drawing and writing.
Key experiences include observing real caterpillars, completing a local walk and exploring maps.
Summer 2: The Seaside, the Natural World and Transition
Children connect and apply their learning with increasing independence.
They explore questions including:
Children compare Westbury with the seaside using first-hand observations, maps and photographs. They investigate how seaside holidays have changed and learn about the marine environment.
Children also reflect upon their Reception journey and prepare positively for their transition to Year 1.
Key experiences include a beach visit and opportunities to become familiar with Year 1.
Learning That Continues Throughout the Year
Across the year, children experience:
daily Read Write Inc. Phonics;
high-quality stories read aloud;
rich conversations, vocabulary, rhyme and poetry;
Mastering Number and practical mathematics;
regular outdoor learning and seasonal observation;
daily movement and frequent physical challenges;
music, movement and imaginative play;
creative exploration;
increasing independence and responsibility; and
Read Write Inc. Phonics
We use Read Write Inc. Phonics to teach reading and writing systematically.
Children learn to recognise sounds, blend sounds to read words and segment words for spelling. They read books closely matched to the sounds they have learned and reread them to develop accuracy, fluency and confidence.
Find out more about Read Write Inc and Writing
https://www.westbury-inf.wilts.sch.uk/Phonics-and-Early-Reading/
https://www.westbury-inf.wilts.sch.uk/Writing/
Mastering Number
We use Mastering Number to help children develop a secure and flexible understanding of number.
Children explore quantities, number composition, numerical relationships and patterns through practical resources, visual representations and mathematical conversations.
Find out more about Mathematics and Mastering Number.
https://www.westbury-inf.wilts.sch.uk/Maths/

Assessment in Reception
Assessment is mainly based on teachers knowing children well.
Adults notice what children know, understand and can do through conversations, observations, play, practical activities, direct teaching and independent work.
This information helps teachers decide what children need to learn next. Assessment should not place unnecessary pressure on children.
At the end of Reception, teachers complete the statutory EYFS Profile. The Early Learning Goals are used as part of this assessment, but they do not represent the complete Reception curriculum or everything children are taught.
Working with Families
Families know their children best. We encourage parents and carers to share their child’s interests, experiences, achievements and needs with us.
Termly Overviews and Building Blocks
At the beginning of each term, we produce a termly overview so families can see the learning, experiences and key texts planned for their child.
We also share our Building Blocks, which explain what we hope children will know, understand and be able to do by the end of the term. These help parents and carers understand how learning develops and identify everyday opportunities to support it at home.
The termly overviews and Building Blocks are shared on our class blog pages.
Kangaroo Class Blogs Koala Class Blogs
Learning Squares
Every child has a Learning Square displayed in the classroom. This celebrates achievements, special experiences and memorable moments from both school and home, helping children feel proud of who they are and what they can do.
Parents and carers can contribute by emailing photographs and a short description to the class email address. This might include:
These contributions help us recognise learning beyond the classroom and give children valuable opportunities to talk about their lives and achievements with others.
Each curriculum-area page also contains practical suggestions for supporting learning at home. These are designed to fit naturally into family life rather than create additional formal work.
If you have questions about your child’s learning, development or wellbeing, please speak to their class teacher.
By working together, we can help every child belong, thrive, achieve and play.

pageCache.text:
Foundation Subjects Progression
At Westbury Infant School, the foundation subjects curriculum is designed around our belief that every child is unique and should be empowered to become a confident, resilient, kind, independent, creative, self-motivated, and active lifelong learner. It is delivered through a broad and balanced curriculum, with opportunities for self-directed learning through play. The curriculum has been developed with a strong understanding of child development research to ensure it meets the needs and learning styles of all our pupils. Knowledge and skills are carefully sequenced, keeping learning simple and focused, and ensuring that what needs to be taught is embedded through regular practice, recognising that practice makes permanent.

Westbury Infant School and Westbury Junior School are proud to partner with Junior Adventures Group (JAG) — the UK's leading provider of before and after-school programmes.
JAG delivers fun, active, and affordable childcare on-site every school day, offering parents convenient, flexible, and reliable wraparound care. All team members are DBS-checked, first-aid qualified, and passionate about creating engaging, safe environments for children to learn and play.

✅ On-site convenience – all sessions take place at school, making drop-offs and pick-ups easy✅ Flexible bookings – cancel or amend bookings up to 48 hours before a session✅ Safe and reliable care – fully trained, trusted staff✅ Healthy and engaging – nutritious snacks and active play every day✅ Something for everyone – a mix of sports, creative activities, and calm spaces for reading or LEGO
🗺️ The Adventure Programme
Every JAG session is designed around the Adventure Programme — a framework of themed activities that encourage learning through play, curiosity, and teamwork.Children can take part in Super Sports, Global Kids, Creative Inventors, Wellbeing Warriors, and more.
